findings.detail: The PR introduces `isNotice` precisely because an app-generated assistant message gets relabelled "Analyst:" by `historyContext` and fed back to the model. The catch block pushes `{ role: 'assistant', content: \`Error: ${e.message}\` }` with no `isNotice`, so it is the one remaining message in this component that the app writes and the model then reads as its own words. After a quota or key failure mid-conversation the next prompt contains `Analyst: Error: API Key required for analysis`, and the model answers with that as context — the exact failure the commit message calls "worse than no notice". The line predates this diff, which is what keeps this out of high; what would raise it is that the error path is not rare (quota and key errors are the common failures here) and the fix is one property.
findings.summary: Error messages still leak into the next prompt as "Analyst:" text

findings.detail: The permanent live region interpolates `${t.actions.noModel}. ${t.actions.noModelHelp}` and the visible panel two lines below renders `t.actions.noModelHelp` again. The comment at line 123-124 says "the text is not announced twice" — that is correct for the *announcement* (only the live region fires), but `sr-only` is a clip technique, not `display:none`, so both copies stay in the accessibility tree. A screen-reader user who Tests, hears the announcement, then browses the dialog to re-read it encounters the help text a second time. Genuinely minor, but it is avoidable by nesting rather than duplicating.
findings.summary: `noModelHelp` now appears twice in the accessibility tree

findings.detail: The other half of this PR fixes exactly this class in ApiKeyModal: a status change that arrives with no live region is invisible to a screen-reader user. "Model changed: … Output quality may differ." is appended into the transcript container at line 672, which has no `role="log"`, `aria-live`, or `role="status"` anywhere — so the one channel this component has to tell the user the model degraded reaches only sighted users. Low rather than high because the container's silence pre-dates this diff (analyst answers already arrive unannounced), so the notice is not a regression; but this PR is the one that adds a *status* message, as distinct from conversational content, and the accessibility handbook § rule 6 covers exactly that.
findings.summary: The fallback notice is never announced — transcript has no live region

findings.detail: The `app` fixture calls `shell.goto()` during setup (e2e/fixtures.ts:86-89), which runs before the test body installs `page.route`. The body then calls `await app.goto()` a second time so the route applies. The spec therefore loads the whole app twice on every run, the first time with no interception, and calls `addInitScript` twice. It passes, but `e2e/fixtures.ts:66` documents `shell` as "the app shell WITHOUT navigating — for tests that control their own load", which is precisely this case; `e2e/responsive.spec.ts` uses it that way throughout.
findings.summary: Uses the `app` fixture then navigates again — one wasted unrouted load

findings.detail: The inlined poll carried `message: 'the sidebar never went off-canvas at 375px'`; the shared helper reports the generic 'the drawer never reached its resting position'. Reusing the helper is the right call and this is not a defect — but this suite is unusually disciplined about failure text (every neighbouring `expect` carries a bespoke message naming the viewport), and `drawerRightEdge` is now used at three call sites that fail for three different reasons. An observation, not a request.
findings.summary: De-duplicating the poll dropped its call-site-specific failure message
